# This fork's (2026-11-26, Retroid Pocket Nova, Adreno 740, 12 GB): the game makes 1,685 MB of NVN memory pools and the GPU uses about 640 MB of them, while the backend gave every
# pool a hardware buffer at creation (memory no swap takes and that only the kernel's Normal zone holds: 7.2 GB of this device's 11.5 GB). With the driver's own allocations
# rising from 1.4 GB at the title to 3.8-4.5 GB while the opening cutscene loads, that zone ran out: the whole device stalled in memory reclaim for 80-135 s (PSI memory "full"
# for 71 of 81 s) until Android's low-memory killer ended the game, 6 runs of 9. MemAvailable stayed at 2.4-4.4 GB throughout, so the backend's own memory pressure levels never
# started. Lazy pools in 32 MB chunks leave a pool on the game's ordinary pages until the GPU first uses it: 370-540 MB of hardware buffers instead of 1,705 MB, and the opening
# cutscene and a save's load into the lobby then ran without a stall
env
env
# This fork's (2026-11-27, Retroid Pocket Nova): magenta and blue dotted lines along every triangle edge in the dark rooms (5F, room 501). The deferred lighting
# shader (fs 55efc9e525f834a3, the first draw of the light pass) takes the screen position of the first lane of each group of four with an indexed shuffle (SHFL.IDX, c 0x1c03), which
# on the console is the top-left pixel of the pixel's 2x2 quad, and read the depth and G-buffer there. Adreno's lanes are not laid out in quads of four in that order:
# at a triangle's edge the light read another surface's G-buffer. As subgroups of one invocation (the same rewrite as Echoes of Wisdom's) each pixel reads its own
# texel; the lines are gone, 30 fps as before
